subject: Re: Post-call: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens (FastRetail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens

Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned.

What we covered (summary):
- FastRetail usage: user-facing conversational flows with high reuse of templated prompts (cart assistants, returns flows).
- Your rough volumes: you said ~50M prompt tokens / month and ~60M completion tokens / month (total ~110M). Peak day ~12-15M tokens.
- Budget: you indicated an initial procurement target of $8k- $12k / month while you validate the integration.
- Pricing ask: you wanted to understand how prefix caching affects effective $/1M tokens and what hit rates we should model for quoting.

Assumptions I’ll start with for an initial pricing worksheet (attached):
- Baseline model price (Redwood blended): $70 per 1M tokens (no caching).
- Prefix cache applies to prompt tokens only; we assume average prompt reduction is proportional to prefix hit rate.
- Sample hit-rate scenarios in the sheet: 25%, 40%, 55% (range we commonly see for templated retail flows).
- Effective $/1M after caching is computed as: effective = baseline * (1 - prompt_token_fraction * hit_rate).
  - For example, if prompts are 45% of total tokens and hit rate is 40%, effective cost ≈ baseline * (1 - 0.45*0.4).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a short worksheet with three hit-rate scenarios and the resulting effective $/1M tokens (attached).
2) If you’re comfortable, can Procurement share an initial target committed volume (1-3 mo) to model committed pricing?
3) We’ll run a 2-week pilot to validate real cache hit rates on your UI flows (we can provide instrumentation and a small sample quota).

Attachments: FR-pricing-cache-assumptions-v1.xlsx (breakdown by prompt vs completion, hit-rate scenarios, recommended target pricing), redwood-pricing-summary.pdf

Thanks — I’m looping Marcus on technical follow-ups.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap and the sheet (downloading now). A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: I checked with engineering — more precise numbers are ~60M prompt tokens / month and ~90M completion tokens / month (total ~150M). Peak daily burst could hit ~20M tokens on promo days.
- Budget: procurement is aiming for an initial pilot budget of $10k/month. If the pilot validates, the long-term budget could expand to $30k- $50k/month depending on results.
- Metric: our CFO cares about an "effective $/1M tokens" metric after caching; target threshold to make this a go is around $40- $60 per 1M tokens for the first 3 months (we can relax later).

Questions: 
1) Are you modeling prompt vs completion split based on our numbers (60/90)?
2) How sensitive is the effective $/1M to hit-rate changes versus model base price? e.g., if hit-rate is only 25% will we still be in the $40- $60 target?

If you can send a scenario table with our exact volumes and the three hit-rate assumptions (25/40/55) that’d be super helpful - procurement will use that in the SOW.

—Samir

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens

Marcus — forwarding Samir's clarification. He gave concrete volumes (60M prompt / 90M completion => 150M total) and a pilot budget $10k/mo. CFO target effective $/1M = $40- $60. Can you quickly validate our worksheet assumptions and call out what hit-rate range is reasonable for their UI?

My quick math (in sheet):
- Baseline blended price: $70 / 1M tokens (no cache) — this uses current model mix and infra.
- Prompt fraction = 60 / 150 = 0.40.
- Effective price formula: effective = baseline * (1 - prompt_fraction * hit_rate).
  - Hit-rate 25% -> effective = 70 * (1 - 0.40*0.25) = 70 * 0.90 = $63 / 1M
  - Hit-rate 40% -> effective = 70 * (1 - 0.40*0.40) = 70 * 0.84 = $58.80 / 1M
  - Hit-rate 55% -> effective = 70 * (1 - 0.40*0.55) = 70 * 0.78 = $54.60 / 1M

Observation: with our baseline $70, even a 55% hit rate only gets to ~$55 / 1M - just inside their upper target. To hit $40 / 1M they'd need either a higher hit rate (>80%) or a lower baseline model price (committed discount / different model).

Recommendation: for the pilot we should: 
- Offer a 20% pilot discount on baseline (effective baseline => $56 / 1M) + assume conservative 40% hit-rate => effective ≈ $47.04 / 1M (falls within their $40- $60 ask).
- Instrument prefix cache metrics and return exact hit-rate after 2 weeks to reprice for commit.

Can you confirm these assumptions (esp. whether prefix cache hits typically reduce only prompt tokens and whether we should account for partial hits due to user-specific variables)? Also call out any changes to the formula if completions can be cached for some flows.

—Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.com>
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens

Samir / Marissa — quick engineering validation and next steps from my side.

1) Cache semantics: prefix caching in your UI will almost exclusively reduce prompt tokens (we cache the tokenized prefix + KV cache where applicable). Completions are rarely cacheable unless the exact input leads to deterministic short answers (some returns-confirmation paths could be cached, but that’s <5% of completions).

2) Hit-rate realism for FastRetail: given your high reuse of templates (cart assistant + returns confirmations + fulfillment status) I expect a steady-state prefix hit-rate in the 35%-50% range after basic normalization (strip user IDs, session tokens). Early pilot may be lower (20%-30%) until we normalize prompts on the frontend.

3) Sensitivity (using their volumes 60M prompts / 90M completions = 150M total):
- Baseline $70 / 1M (no discount):
  - 25% hit -> effective ~$63 / 1M
  - 40% hit -> effective ~$58.80 / 1M
  - 55% hit -> effective ~$54.60 / 1M
- If we apply a 20% pilot discount -> baseline becomes $56 / 1M:
  - 40% hit -> effective ~$47.04 / 1M (meets Samir’s target band)

4) Proposal and next steps:
- Marissa to propose a pilot SOW: 2-week instrumentation + 1-month trial (10k/mo budget) with a 20% pilot discount and an option to convert to a committed 12-month volume with deeper discounts once hit-rate is validated.
- Engineering: we’ll provide a short instrumentation plan + a small sample dataset to run a cache-hit simulation before the pilot; should take <5 engineering days to ship.

I’ll add a tab in the attached workbook with expected daily variations and the simulation parameters.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
